sallylunn_baker.text: Mind your head on the beams. This house is ancient.
It dates from about 1482, so it is one of the oldest houses in Bath. Downstairs, the kitchen museum shows Roman and medieval foundations.
The bun is named for Sally Lunn, a French refugee who may have baked them in the 1680s. Or it came from 'soleil et lune'. Nobody agrees.

then.text: One cup per customer, I am afraid. The beams are still very low, though.

else.text: Have a cup of tea for the road. It is hot, so blow on it before you panic.

then.text: Jam first. Always jam first. Fancy a go at my oven?

else.text: Mind the flour. Everything in here is flour. I am at least forty per cent flour.
You've got blackberries on your fingers. Forager, are we? Then you want a proper cream tea.
Hedgerow jam, a splash of elderflower, scones like clouds. Jam first, cream second. We are in Bath, not Devon, and I'll not be told.
Pop in whenever you've got the makings. You can use my kitchen.
